$BTC slipped to $80,315, down 0.43% after hitting a high of $81,033 and a low of $79,221. Volume held near 9.7k, so the move felt more like a brief wobble than a panic.

Meanwhile $ERA slid 19% to $0.0724, barely touching its $0.071 low and dragging $20.7 M in volume. The winners are blasting past yesterday's ranges, the loser is stuck in a steep dip. In short: $ETH is losing relative strength to $BTC, but the broader alt slice is holding its own and actually beat $BTC's modest dip. Nothing wild, just a small tilt toward the rest of the market.

$BMT surged 67.5% to $0.039, trading in a tight $0.021-$0.051 range and pulling in over $53.9M in quote volume. $ERA also climbed, up about 20.5% to $0.0876, with a high of $0.1031 and $27.2M flowing through. Meanwhile $WLD slipped 12.6% to $0.4636, barely breaking its $0.457-$0.535 band despite the biggest quote volume at $79.6M. Gains on the upside, losses on the downside, just how the 24-hour story unfolded.

$BTC slid 1.28% to $80,662, touching a high of $82,060 before drifting down to a low of $80,451. Volume held around 11.6 k coins, so the sell pressure was clear.

All three pairs nudged lower in the last 24 h, each testing their day's range. No big spikes, just a steady slide across the board.

$PEPE's barely creeping up, +1.34% to $0.00000454, volume over $111 M, while $BNB nudged +0.51% to $739.81 on $106 M traded. On the flip side $WLD slammed –13.88% to $0.4795, volume $67 M, still stuck near its low of $0.4711. One side inching higher, the other diving hard. Looks like the meme-coin rally isn't spilling over to the broader market right now.

$ETH is pulling ahead of $BTC, up 0.546% in BTC terms. $BTC slipped 0.071% over the last 24 h. The 20-coin basket of top alts posted a 0.474% gain, so the average alt is outpacing $BTC. In short, ETH's got relative strength, BTC's lagging, and the broader alt set is nudging ahead of the king. Nothing wild, just a modest shift in the hierarchy.

$BTC stuck around $81,642, up just 0.09% in 24h. It bounced between $80,940 low and $82,061 high, so the range stayed tight.

$ETH nudged to $2,405, a 0.39% gain, trading its day's swing from $2,360 low up to $2,418 high. Volume held strong around 306 k.

All three held above yesterday's lows, no crazy spikes. Just a modest climb for BNB and flatlines for BTC and ETH.

$PEPE bounced hard, climbing to $0.00000495 with a 14.34% swing, almost double its normal 7.38% spread, that's a noticeably wider move.

$BNB nudged up to $745.35, moving 3.17% in 24 h, a bit wider than its average 2.25% range.

All three tokens showed more volatility than they normally do, but none broke the market wide open. Just a lively 24-hour spread.

$AIUSDT pumped 6.77% to $0.0205, hitting a high of $0.0214 before easing back. $TRXUSDT barely budged, down 0.36% at $0.3293, its range stuck between $0.3277 and $0.3314. Meanwhile $SOXLBUSDT took a tumble, sliding 12.77% to $84.33 after flirting with $96.73 earlier. Volume stayed hefty on all three, with $AIUSDT leading the pack. Looks like the AI token is the only one pulling ahead while the index-linked pair is left in the dust.

$BTC slipped 3.75% to $81,357, hugging its 24-hr low of $80,939 after a brief rally up to $84,847. Volume held near 20k BTC, so the move had decent heft.

$ETH fell 4.26% to $2,385, testing the $2,360 floor before bouncing to a high of $2,502. Roughly 266k ETH traded, pushing quote volume past $642 M.

$BNB dropped 2.40% to $731, skimming the $726 support line after peaking at $751. About 107k BNB changed hands, with $78.9 M in quote volume.

All three slid under their highs, so keep an eye on whether they respect the current lows before any fresh push.

$ETH is losing a hair against $BTC, down 0.945% on the ETH/BTC pair (now around 0.02936 BTC). Meanwhile $BTC slipped 3.602% in the last 24 h. The 20-coin basket of top alts fell even harder, down about 7.52% on average. So BTC's outpacing the alt basket, but ETH's still holding a bit more relative strength versus BTC. Overall a pretty bearish day across the board.

$BTC slid to $81,891.79, down 1.85% in 24 h, after hitting a high of $84,898 and finding support near $81,653. $ETH fell 2.36% to $2,402.98, its range squeezed between $2,526.62 and $2,395.55. $BNB dropped 1.71% to $734.04, pulling back from a peak of $751.86 while staying above $730.35. Volume was solid on all three, $BTC around 21.9 k, $ETH about 309 k, $BNB 124.6 k, so liquidity held up. Keep an eye on whether the lows hold; any break back above the recent highs could shift the vibe. No fireworks, just a steady pull-back across the board.

$ALT surged 20.5% to $0.01213, hitting a high of $0.01562 after a swing from $0.00949. Meanwhile $SOXL slipped 8.3% down to $96.46, barely touching its low of $96.3 despite a $106.1 peak. $ZEC nudged up 2.7% to $1,297.33, staying inside a $1250.66-$1368.4 range. Leaders climbing, laggards tumbling, just how the 24-hour dance played out.

$SPCXBUSDT ripped through a 10.11% swing in the last 24 h, almost double its typical 5.96% daily band, that's noticeably wider than usual.

NEAR's move was a bit more tame: it bounced around a 10.96% range, just a shade above its 9.73% norm, so it didn't really break any molds.

Overall, the market's been jittery but nothing crazy beyond the SPCX buzz.

$BTC jumped 2.8% in 24 h, but the 20-coin basket rallied 8.23%, so the alts outpaced the king. $ETH nudged 0.37% higher against $BTC, meaning it's picking up a bit of relative strength. Overall, BTC's still the big mover, yet the broader market is pulling ahead. Nothing wild, just the usual spread between the flagship and the rest.

$IOST exploded, up almost 78% to $0.00143, trading between $0.00078 and $0.00159 with over $33 M in quote volume. $ZEC kept the rally going, +12.9% to $1,284, swinging from $1,135 to $1,296 and pulling in $227 M. Meanwhile $BTC barely budged, +2.4% to $83,442, range $81,322-$83,714 on a $1.12 B volume. The top gainers are blasting off while BTC's just inching forward. Looks like the alt-heavy side got the party started, and BTC's the slow-poke of the day.

$BTC's at $82,760, up 1.35% in 24 h. It bounced from a low of $81,322 to a high of $83,439, holding near the top of that range.

$ETH climbed 2.13% to $2,447.23, swinging between $2,377.6 and $2,478. Volume spiked past 238 k, showing solid hands on the move.

$BNB nudged 1.55% to $740.29, trading inside $727-$744.5. With about 93 k coins changing hands, it's edging higher but still tight.

All three sat in modest upside bands; watch if any breaks past the day highs for the next push.

$BNB slipped up a touch, ending the day at $739.39 with a 1.43% gain. Its 24-hour swing was roughly 2.3%, a shade narrower than the typical 2.6% swing it sees each day, about a tenth tighter than normal.

$SOL nudged higher to $106, up 1.27%. The token's price moved within a 4.32% band, compared with its usual 4.69% range, so the day was just a bit more confined than usual.

All three moved within roughly their usual volatility envelope, nothing wild on the chart.

$BTC's at $82,669.52, up 0.94% in 24 h. It nudged a high of $83,439 before slipping to a low of $81,200, so the range stayed tight.

$BNB pushed up to $735.60, +1.48%, with a swing between $724.86 and $741.99. Trade flow was solid, 88k units changing hands and $64.5 M in quote volume.

All three sat in modest gains, holding near their daily highs. No wild swings, just a calm push higher across the board.

$BTC slipped to $81,490, down 0.9% in 24 h, after hitting a high of $82,757 and testing $81,200 on the lows. Volume hovered around 11.8 k coins, so the move wasn't a flash crash, just a modest pullback.

All three are sitting near their day lows; nothing wild, just a calm shift lower for the majors and a tiny bounce for BNB. Keep an eye on how the volumes hold up.

$BTC slipped to $81,700.38, down 0.85% in 24 h, after hitting a high of $83,158 and a low of $81,200. Volume sat around 12.5 k BTC, roughly $1.03 bn in quote.

$BNB edged up to $728.89, up 0.41%, after a brief run to $733.64 and a dip to $723.19. Volume was 100.97 k BNB, roughly $73.4 m quoted.

All three sat in tight ranges after modest moves; keep an eye on how the next price bars sit relative to those highs and lows. No wild swings today.

Watch the $BNB order flow around the $730 level, any break could set the tone for the next session.
